```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
library(rSDP)
```

## What this is

Bugs and feature requests for the **rSDP package itself** live at
<https://github.com/rmbl-sdp/rSDP/issues>. Issues with the **data products**
served by the Spatial Data Platform — incorrect pixel values, missing dates,
metadata errors, acquisition gaps, documentation problems — live in a
separate repository: <https://github.com/rmbl-sdp/sdp-products>.

Keeping the two separate makes it easier to triage each kind of feedback and
to surface known dataset problems back to other users.

## Reporting an issue

The easiest way is from R, with the dataset's CatalogID in hand:

```{r}
sdp_report_issue("R4D004")
```

That opens your browser to the [Issue Form](https://github.com/rmbl-sdp/sdp-products/issues/new?template=dataset-issue.yml)
with the CatalogID pre-filled. Fill in the remaining structured fields
(issue type, severity, what you observed, what you expected, how to
reproduce) and submit.

You can also pre-fill the issue type:

```{r}
sdp_report_issue("R3D009", type = "metadata-error")
```

Valid types: `incorrect-values`, `missing-dates`, `metadata-error`,
`acquisition-gap`, `documentation`, `other`.

A validation bot will comment within a minute if the CatalogID isn't
recognized, and it auto-applies `product:<CATID>`, `type:<...>`, and
`severity:<...>` labels. A maintainer then reviews and either confirms,
asks for more information, declines to fix it, or resolves the issue.

## Checking for known issues

Before reporting, see if your problem is already known:

```{r}
sdp_known_issues("R4D004")
```

Returns a data frame of open issues for that CatalogID: number, title, type,
severity, status, dates, and URL. Pass no argument to get every open issue
across all datasets.

Results are cached on disk for an hour to keep interactive use responsive
and to stay within GitHub's anonymous rate limit. Pass `refresh = TRUE` to
force a re-fetch.

```{r}
sdp_known_issues(refresh = TRUE)
```

If you have a GitHub Personal Access Token in `GITHUB_PAT` or
`GITHUB_TOKEN`, rSDP will use it for the API call (higher rate limit), but
this is optional — the public endpoint works without auth.

## Surfacing issue counts in catalog browsing

The catalog can carry an open-issue count per dataset:

```{r}
cat <- sdp_get_catalog(with_issue_counts = TRUE)
head(cat[cat$OpenIssues > 0, c("CatalogID", "Product", "OpenIssues")])
```

`sdp_browse()` renders the same information as a small "⚠ N open issues"
badge on each card:

```{r}
sdp_browse(types = "Snow", with_issue_counts = TRUE)
```

The badge links straight to the filtered open-issues view on GitHub, so
clicking it shows the actual tickets.

## In the STAC catalog

The static STAC catalog at
`s3://rmbl-sdp/stac/v1/` carries the same information on every collection:

- `rmbl:open_issues_count` — number of open issues for the dataset
- A `report-issue` rel link to the prefilled new-issue form
- A `related` rel link to the filtered open-issues list

The count is refreshed within ~30 seconds of any issue event (open, close,
relabel) via a GitHub Actions workflow on `rmbl-sdp/sdp-products`, so STAC
Browser and other clients see fresh numbers without waiting for a full
catalog rebuild.

## Without a GitHub account

Right now, filing an issue requires a GitHub account. We may add a no-auth
intake form (`rmbl.org/sdp/report-issue/`) if the GitHub-account barrier
turns out to be a real friction point for the community. If you'd rather
email about a dataset problem, write to <support@rmbl.org> and we'll file
the issue on your behalf.
